plain: Pick a spot that gets at least six to eight hours of direct sun daily, and amend your soil with compost since tomatoes are heavy feeders. Choose a mix of determinate varieties for a compact harvest and indeterminate ones for a longer season, and start from transplants rather than seed if your season is short. Space plants 18-24 inches apart, stake or cage them early, and water deeply but infrequently at the base to encourage strong roots and avoid fungal issues. Mulch to retain moisture, pinch off suckers on indeterminate plants, and feed every few weeks with a balanced or tomato-specific fertilizer.

plain: San Diego has plenty of kid-friendly spots. The San Diego Zoo and Safari Park are classics, with hundreds of species and interactive exhibits. SeaWorld offers marine shows and rides suited for younger kids. Balboa Park is great for a low-key day, with museums, gardens, and open lawns to run around on. The USS Midway Museum lets kids climb through a real aircraft carrier, and LEGOLAND California is built specifically for younger children. For beach time, Coronado Beach and Mission Bay Park have calm water and playgrounds nearby. Old Town San Diego is fun for food and a bit of history too.

Each has its own character, so it's worth visiting more than one if you have time.

plain: The loquat is a small, orange to yellow fruit with a sweet-tart flavor, somewhere between a plum and a mild citrus. It grows on an evergreen tree and has smooth or slightly fuzzy skin with a few large seeds inside. Loquats originated in southeastern China, in the cooler hill regions, and have been cultivated there for over a thousand years. From China the tree spread to Japan, where it's also widely grown, and later to the Mediterranean, India, and parts of the Americas. Today it's popular in home gardens because the tree is hardy and produces fruit early in spring, often before other fruit trees even blossom.

plain: A traditional sauna centers on a heat source, usually a wood-burning or electric stove topped with rocks, which brings the room to somewhere between 150-195F. Good insulation and wood paneling (often spruce or cedar) help the room hold heat evenly and stay comfortable to sit in. Ventilation matters too, since fresh air needs to circulate without cooling the room too much. Benches at different heights let people choose their preferred heat level, since it's hotter higher up. Water poured over the hot rocks creates steam and a burst of humidity, and many saunas include a way to cool down afterward, like a cold plunge or shower.

plain: Start by getting a permit early, since backcountry permits for the Grand Canyon are limited and often booked months ahead. Pick a route based on your experience -- the Bright Angel or South Kaibab trails are well-maintained and good for beginners, while inner canyon routes like the Tonto Trail are more remote. Plan around water sources carefully, since many are seasonal, and carry more than you think you'll need. Train beforehand for steep, sustained elevation changes, since the return climb is brutal in heat. Go in spring or fall to avoid extreme summer temperatures, pack a reliable water filter, sun protection, and a headlamp, and always check current trail and water conditions with the park's backcountry office before you go.

plain: Mogul skiing puts repeated, forceful compression on your spine as you absorb bump after bump, especially if you're using your back to soak up impact instead of your legs and hips. If your core is weak, your lower back ends up doing work it isn't built for, leading to strain or spasm. Poor absorption technique -- stiff legs, skiing too fast for your skill level, or leaning back on your skis -- also transfers more shock straight into your spine. Fatigue makes it worse, since tired muscles stabilize less and let more force through. Strengthening your core and hip flexors, practicing softer knee and ankle flexion to absorb bumps, and pacing yourself on long mogul runs can all reduce the strain.

plain: Audiophiles chase incremental improvements in clarity, soundstage, and tonal accuracy that become harder and more expensive to achieve as you approach the upper limits of what's audibly perceptible. Better components -- DACs, amplifiers, speakers, cables to a lesser extent -- can reduce distortion, noise, and frequency response irregularities, and some listeners are genuinely sensitive to these differences. But no, more expensive doesn't always mean better sound. Diminishing returns set in hard past a certain price point, room acoustics and source material quality often matter more than gear, and some premium products rely more on branding and subjective preference than measurable performance. A well-chosen mid-range setup in a treated room frequently outperforms poorly matched expensive gear.

plain: Try dishes that let picky eaters customize their own plate. Build-your-own veggie quesadillas or tacos work well since kids can pick their fillings and skip what they don't like. Homemade pizza with a plain cheese base and toppings on the side is another easy win. Veggie fried rice, where you cook the vegetables small and mix them in gradually, can sneak in nutrition without an obvious pile of vegetables. Bean and cheese quesadillas, mac and cheese with hidden pureed squash or carrots, and breakfast-for-dinner options like veggie omelets or pancakes with fruit also tend to go over well with reluctant young eaters.

plain: The most immediate difference is humidity -- Miami's heat is thick and tropical year-round, nothing like California's dry heat, and afternoon thunderstorms in summer are routine. Beaches are flatter and warmer, without the surf culture or cliffs common in coastal California.
